summary.short: Oregon Senate Bill 619 (2023) enacts the Oregon Consumer Privacy Act, operative July 1, 2024. It imposes consumer data rights and controller and processor duties on businesses serving Oregon above volume thresholds, enforced by the Attorney General.
summary.long: Oregon Senate Bill 619 (2023) enacts the Oregon Consumer Privacy Act, operative July 1, 2024. It applies to businesses serving Oregon that process personal data of 100,000 or more consumers a year, or 25,000 or more while earning 25 percent of gross revenue from data sales. Consumers may access, correct, delete and port their personal data and opt out of targeted advertising, data sales and certain profiling. Controllers must give a privacy notice, limit collection and use to disclosed purposes, obtain consent for sensitive data, avoid discriminating against consumers who exercise rights, and conduct data protection assessments for heightened-risk processing; responses are due within 45 days. Processors must follow controller instructions under contract. The Attorney General enforces with investigative demands and civil penalties of up to $7,500 per violation after a 30-day cure notice; no private right of action exists. Many exemptions apply, including HIPAA and financial institutions. From January 1, 2026, the cure notice is removed and controllers must allow universal opt-out signals.

notes: No legal_basis relation: the text cites no enabling act. Enrolled text (SB 619-B) with blank signature lines and no chapter number or signing date; the in_force status rests on registry metadata. Internal inconsistency in timing: Section 15(1) makes Sections 1 to 9 and the ORS 180.095 amendment operative July 1, 2024, while Sections 11 and 12 (restating Sections 9 and 5 with bracketed deletions) are operative January 1, 2026 under Section 15(2)-(3), so the text contains two operative versions of Sections 5 and 9. The Section 11 version deletes the 30-day cure notice in former Section 9(5). Section 14 is garbled by the source layout ('limitation on ex, Oregon Laws 2023 (Enrolled Senpenditures...'), so its intended wording cannot be reconstructed. Other ORS and federal references in Sections 1 and 2(2) (e.g., ORS 706.008, 725.010, 731.106) are not listed individually.
